body: I think a solution could be to add all non-producer beans first.

Well, actually this would not help if there are normal scoped producers that depend on each other, or? This is the reason why I believe the circular dependencies are wrong. @manovotn  @mthmulders Any ideas how to fix this?
In fact, it wouldn't be enough even for the simple use case. We would have to make use of `javax.enterprise.context.spi.CreationalContext.push(T)` for the producers :-(.

I don't really like circular deps either, but CDI specifcation says it should work (in certain circumstances)...

Anyway, a few lines below the one that you've linked, we create a `MapBeanSupplier` and give it both the map of `Suppliers` and an identifier for the bean to be resolved. Maybe we should do the same thing for producer methods and fields?

If we could have a test case for this, it would be easier to validate this approach. The `MPConfigBean` is depends on MicroProfile so we can't just copy-paste it...

Thanks Maarten.

1. producers == beans and we do put them in the map too.
2. The validation part is not a problem. The real problem is when such beans are instantiated at runtime.

I'm going to create a test and I'll post the branch link here so that it's easy to reproduce.
For the record, master branch of MP CP doesn't have circular deps anymore and the error is the same.

I've checked out your branch, Martin.

The testcase with the class that consumes a bean it produces succeeds on my machine. Also, the other testcases succeed. Does that mean you've already fixed the issue or am I overseeing something?
I fixed one issue but there are certainly other corner cases that are not covered. In any case, I'm going to send a PR and we can continue improving the code ;-). Thanks a lot for the feedback.

issue.title: Fix NPE when handling circular dependencies

body: Thanks for having a fix ready even before I could start to think of one :-)
